title: Revamp model indexing API: advanced filtering, compat flags, and per-model pricing/rate fields
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: product teams are asking for a single model index endpoint that supports precise filtering by runtime capabilities (streaming, function/tool-calling, structured output) and also surface per-model pricing and rate-limit metadata to make routing and cost-aware routing decisions on the client side. The current /models catalog is inconsistent across SDKs and the OpenAI-compat layer omits several capability flags used by our runtime. This PR introduces a v2 model index API, enriches each model entry with capability flags, per-model pricing/rate settings, and expands OpenAI compatibility mappings.

Summary of changes: added /v2/models/index endpoint that supports query parameters: capability, price_max, region, compatibility=true/false, and sort_by=latency|price. Each model entry now includes booleans for streaming_supported, function_calling_supported, structured_output_supported, openai_compat (enum: partial|full|none), and fields unit_price_usd_per_1k_tokens, rps_limit, burst_capacity. The OpenAI compatibility layer now maps function-calling hooks to our tool-calling runtime and exposes compat notes when model behavior differs.

Checklist: 
- [x] API schema and OpenAPI docs updated (docs/api/model_catalog.md)
- [x] SDK surface (python/typescript) updated with wrappers for new endpoint
- [x] Backwards-compatible: original /models returns unchanged minimal entries; v2 is opt-in
- [x] Tests added: unit + integration against local runtime catalog fixture
- [x] Performance: endpoint paginates and supports light-weight indexing to meet SLOs

Compatibility/migration notes: clients should opt into /v2/models/index to receive pricing and rate fields. Old fields are kept for compatibility; however the openai_compat enum semantics are expanded — see docs for mapping. SDKs provide helper methods to translate v2 entries into legacy shapes for quick migration.

Why not just extend /models? We kept the original endpoint stable to avoid accidental selector breakage in customers' code; v2 permits experimental additions and richer metadata without breaking existing clients.

Links: Linear ENG-3176 (model index revamp); SUP-2241 incident context where customers wanted programmatic pricing selection.

Test plan: unit tests for JSON schema validation, mocked catalog + end-to-end integration test that asserts filtering by capability and price produces expected results, load test to ensure latency stays within 50ms p95 for the first page with 1000 concurrent requests (mocked cache).

review_thread: Marco Li: Please add a short note in migration docs that SDKs will default to legacy /models until a flag is flipped. — PRIYA: added paragraph under 'Compatibility/migration notes' in the PR description and updated SDKs to default to legacy behavior.

Ava Thompson: The rps_limit field is an integer but should we support per-tenant overrides? Consider naming it rps_default. — PRIYA: renamed internal field to rps_default and added optional tenant_overrides map in the registry (tenant_overrides left internal, not exposed in the public model list).
Jordan Kim: CI flaked on integration test once; can you make sure the fixture seed is deterministic? — PRIYA: fixed test seed and added a repeatable fixture generator.
checks_summary: unit-tests: pass (pkg: 98.7% coverage for changed files)
e2e-load-smoke: pass after increasing index cache TTL
release_notes: Added v2 model index endpoint (/v2/models/index) with advanced filtering and enriched model metadata: streaming_supported, function_calling_supported, structured_output_supported, openai_compat (partial|full|none), unit_price_usd_per_1k_tokens, rps_default, burst_capacity. Old /models remains unchanged. SDKs updated to expose new helper methods.
migration_notes: Clients that need pricing or capability-rich responses should call /v2/models/index. SDKs expose ModelIndexV2 and a to_legacy() helper for quick conversion. If you relied on implicit ordering, migrate to explicit sort_by param. No forced migration required.
test_plan: Run unit + integration suite. Manual smoke: curl /v2/models/index?capability=streaming&price_max=0.05 and assert returned models have streaming_supported=true and unit_price_usd_per_1k_tokens<=0.05. Verify SDK wrappers return paginated results and preserve legacy compatibility when using default client settings.
notes_for_backport: No; v2 is additive. Backport not required. If backporting to release/* for customers on dedicated instances, strip pricing fields tied to cloud-only billing (backport PR should remove unit_price_usd_per_1k_tokens).
